date_note: Iran International published on 21 November; the approaches happened over earlier months and the article gives no date for them.
title: Australian broadcaster Erin Molan says Iran-linked hackers posed as a US expert to target her
summary: Iran International reports that broadcaster Erin Molan says someone using a real US think-tank expert's name contacted her on X, and that she later clicked a meeting link and found a security breach alert on her account. She says ASIO's head told her she was one of three Australians targeted and that the operation was linked to Iran. Journalist Sharri Markson told NewsNation that Australian intelligence officials linked it to Charming Kitten.
plain: An Australian broadcaster says she was approached by someone posing as a US expert and later found a breach alert on her account. She says Australian officials linked it to Iran.
exec: Impersonation of trusted contacts to reach media figures; the Iran link rests on the targets' accounts of what officials told them.
action: Verify any meeting invitation from a new contact through a second channel before clicking its link, and check account security alerts.

validation.note: Only Iran International read. Attribution comes from Molan and Markson relaying what ASIO and Australian intelligence officials told them; no ASIO statement read.
